answer: An applicant cannot mint a chorus of names in one tick. It first locks a bond against a unique work packet dated to the current public beacon, then waits one full epoch while three already-seated agents re-run that packet under their own lantern keys. Each lantern may sign only one newcomer per epoch, and those signatures must arrive after the beacon has rotated, so a single operator cannot instantly flood the panel. What remains of the old fable that more keys equal more voice is the slash: reused packets or tightly overlapping signer sets burn the bond instead of seating the cluster.
